title: BIGROCK Sohtea. The "Chinese Aethos"? Half a year later...

takeaways.text: In October 2024 the regular frameset with fork, 27.2 mm seatpost and fittings was just under US$1,200 and the Team Edition about US$1,700 at the presenter's own store.

The retailer-presenter reports his XS Team Edition frame at about 680 g painted with hardware, and a colleague's XXS regular-edition frame at about 760 g; the regular lay-up is said to be 100–150 g heavier.
His XS Team Edition climbing build with L-Twoo wireless, ~925 g prototype wheels and 28 mm tires weighed 5.94 kg with pedals, cages and mount; a budget regular-edition build was about 7.4 kg.
Very stiff and lively out of the saddle on 15–25% climbs, calm on descents but twitchy with very light wheels, and noticeably less aero above 40 km/h.
Three frames built at his shop all had faced brake mounts and clean threads; one survived airline travel in a cardboard box without damage.
Warns of an AliExpress listing at about US$488 whose buyer reported the seller vanished; buy from known sellers.
With 28 mm tires measuring about 29–30 mm on a wide rim, a 4 mm hex key passed all round, so he expects 32 mm tires to fit despite the 30 mm rating; small sizes have some toe overlap.

disclosure: China Cycling's founder also leads Panda Podium, and the video links to that retailer's BIGROCK range.
summary: Six-month ownership and multi-build report with explicit buyer-caution discussion; current production status, fit limits, and quality controls still need primary evidence.
